verses.text: For the music director. A psalm by the sons of Korah. Hear this, all you peoples. Listen, everyone who lives in the world,
people of high and low standing, rich and poor alike.
I’ll speak words of wisdom. What I’ve thought through in my heart will give understanding.
I’ll listen closely to a proverb and explain my riddle to the sound of the harp.
Why should I be afraid when trouble comes and the evil of those at my heels closes in around me?
Some people trust in their wealth and boast about how much they own,
yet none of them can buy back the life of another or pay God a ransom for them.
The price of a life is too high. No payment is ever enough
to let someone live forever and never see decay.
Everyone can see that wise people die. Fools and the senseless die too, leaving their wealth to others.
They imagine their houses will stand forever, with descendants living there generation after generation. They name their lands after themselves.
But even with all their wealth, people don’t last. They die just like animals.
That’s the fate of those who live foolishly and of those who applaud what they say. Selah.
They’re like sheep marked for Sheol, with death as their shepherd. In the morning the upright will rule over them. Their beauty will decay in Sheol, far from their grand homes.
But God will rescue my life from the power of Sheol, because he’ll take me in. Selah.
Don’t be afraid when someone grows rich and their household grows more impressive.
When they die, they’ll take nothing with them. Their glory won’t follow them down.
They may congratulate themselves while they’re alive, and people may praise you when you do well for yourself,
but they’ll join their ancestors, who will never see the light again.
People who have wealth without understanding are like animals that perish.
